name: libwbxml
desc: Library and tools to parse and encode WBXML documents
why: Parses WAP Binary XML, a door into the old mobile protocol world of compact encoded XML used by phones for sync.

brief.what_it_is: libwbxml is a C library and two command-line tools for working with WBXML, the WAP Binary XML format. The library parses WBXML documents, builds an internal tree, and encodes that tree back out. The tools are wbxml2xml, which takes a WBXML file and writes readable XML, and xml2wbxml, which takes an XML file and writes WBXML. The README describes the library as a SAX-like parser, so it works like Expat but for WBXML.
brief.why_it_exists: The README says WBXML is a binary representation of XML, defined by the WAP Forum and used to reduce bandwidth in mobile communications. The library exists to read and write that format, and it covers many WAP-era document languages such as WML, SyncML, and OTA settings.
brief.how_it_works: Input goes through either the WBXML parser or the Expat XML parser, and both feed a common WBXML Tree structure. The WBXML Encoder then writes that tree out as WBXML or as XML. The README calls the XML side Expat-based, so XML parsing depends on that library.

commands_seen.context: Basic WBXML-to-XML conversion example from the README, writing output.xml. The bare -i appears as written in the README.
Converts WBXML to XML with an indent delta of 4 and forces the document language to WV CSP 1.2 using -l CSP12.
Basic XML-to-WBXML conversion example from the README, writing output.wbxml.
Converts XML to WBXML with whitespace kept (-k), no string table generated (-n), and WBXML version 1.1 output (-v 1.1).

brief.install_notes: The README gives no install steps beyond the Homebrew formula. It says the library needs Expat to enable XML parsing, which means XML-to-WBXML conversion needs Expat available. No accounts, hardware, or first-run configuration are mentioned.
brief.standout: It covers a niche protocol family, WAP-era WBXML with many document languages, and it is a full round-trip toolkit with a library API and CLI tools. The SAX-style parser and the shared tree between the two directions are a tidy design for a binary format.
brief.status: unknown. The README does not give a version number or date. It says releases are published only on GitHub and that bugs are taken there, which suggests the project is still active, but I did not see a commit date or release date in what I read.
brief.caveats: Requires Expat for XML parsing. Several language entries are marked only as tested or partially tested, and WV CSP 1.2 is marked partially tested. The -l option list pairs SI10 with 'SL 1.0' and SL10 with 'SI 1.0', which looks swapped, so check before relying on it. The README gives no license information and no build instructions. The -i flag is shown in the README without a value in one example, so the usage is ambiguous.
quotes: The WBXML format is a binary representation of XML, defined by the Wap Forum, and used to reduce bandwidth in mobile communications.
The WBXML Library needs Expat to enable XML Parsing feature (and so XML to WBXML conversion).
Today, releases are only published on GitHub.

judge.reason: WBXML’s compact, tokenized form of XML opens a small window into WAP-era protocols, and these tools let you inspect and round-trip it.

entry.title: libwbxml
entry.tldr: A C library and two converters for WBXML, the compact binary XML that WAP-era phones used for settings, sync and messages.
entry.deeper_look:
WBXML is a binary encoding of XML, defined by the WAP Forum. In the project's words, it is "used to reduce bandwidth in mobile communications." Instead of spelling out tags as text, it swaps them for single-byte tokens, which mattered a great deal on slow early mobile links.

libwbxml reads and writes that format. It ships two tools: wbxml2xml turns a WBXML file into readable XML, and xml2wbxml goes the other way. The library behind them covers many WAP-era document languages, including WML, SyncML and OTA settings.

The design is tidy. Input goes through either a WBXML parser or the Expat XML parser, and both build the same in-memory tree. An encoder then writes that tree out as WBXML or as XML. The README describes the parser as SAX-like, in the spirit of Expat but for WBXML.

The idea underneath is that a token table agreed in advance can stand in for text. Decoding a WBXML blob means knowing which document language it uses, and the tools let you force one with a flag when it is not obvious. It is a small window into how phones once synced contacts and received settings over very thin pipes.
entry.install:
brew install libwbxml
# XML-to-WBXML conversion depends on Expat being available

try_this.what_happens: Decodes a WBXML file into readable XML written to output.xml. The README example also shows a bare -i, but its usage is ambiguous there.
Encodes an XML file as WBXML.
Encodes to WBXML version 1.1, keeping whitespace and skipping the string table.

entry.whats_unique: It is a full round-trip toolkit for a niche protocol family, with a library API and command-line tools sharing one tree structure. Few tools can read or write this format at all.
entry.caveats: The README gives no version or date and lists several document languages as only tested or partially tested; the -l option table also looks to have SI10 and SL10 swapped, so check before relying on it.
